extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, agents, inventors, and legal practitioners working on patents, designs and trade marks (United Kingdom)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for applying, registering, renewing, enforcing and challenging patents, designs and trade marks under the Acts and Rules referenced (UK, Designs/Patents/Trade Marks practice). Includes required forms, time limits, evidentiary rules and remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of Patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Fourteen years from date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Term ceases on failure to make prescribed payment. Notice of renewal to be given. Enlargement of time for payment not to exceed three months; fees for extension; infringements during extended time are addressed. (References: 25–26; application form for extension, 200.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal — Patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual fees may be paid; enlargement of time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules govern payment of renewal fees and enlargement of time for payments (see sections cited at 25–26).

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal — Trade Mark Registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration of a Trade Mark every fourteen years; mark removed 3 months after expiration if fee not paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional fee payable if fee is paid after the period has expired; after removal a mark may be restored. Extension of time provisions apply. (Refs: 111–112.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Sealing of Patent / Seal of Patent Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters Patent sealed with the seal of the Patent Office; this seal substituted for the Great Seal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time of sealing: within 15 months of date of application except (1) where appeal pending to law officer, (2) where applicant dies (Patent may be sealed within 12 months of death). Sealing not to prevent sealing of Patent on prior application. Impressions of the seal are judicially noticed; copies sealed and certified are receivable in evidence. (Refs: 20, 121–122.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Report of Examiner (Patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report as to an application for a Patent, on what matters and as to identity of two applications; as to comparison of complete with provisional specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports indicate how far conclusive they are; reports not to be open to public inspection nor to production or inspection in legal proceedings except on appeal to law officer or where ordered. (Refs: 9, 10, 14–15.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Representations / Specimens to accompany applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Representations of a Design may accompany application to register; exact representations or specimens to be furnished before delivery of articles on sale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules, instructions and requirements as to number and size of representations for Designs and Trade Marks are specified (see Drawings; representations for Trade Mark application: 86, 236–256; for Design: 74, 210, 219). Wood-blocks/electrotypes and tracings may be required; instructions given at cited pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on Registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain marks are not entitled to registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trade Marks not entitled to registration if already registered, if calculated to deceive, if scandalous, if contrary to law or morality, or if not coming within the statutory definition. Common marks may be registered as an addition. Marks must be registered for a class (or part) of goods. (Refs: 89–103, 122; see 95 for series and class rules.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation of a Patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceeding by scire facias abolished; revocation now obtained by petition to the Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Who may present petition and particulars of objections must be set out. Amendment of specification may be allowed at hearing. Defendant begins at hearing. Where Patent revoked for fraud a new Patent may be granted but to expire when revoked Patent would have expired. Revocation order to be entered on the register and left. (Refs: 41–45, 35–36.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Searches (Designs and Trade Marks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Search as to existence of copyright in a Design; search as to a Trade Mark being registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form of request and fee for searches specified. Instructions as to searches appear and searches may be conducted by the Comptroller. (Refs: 78, 215, 221, 255.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheffield Marks (special regime)
rubrics_metrics.description: Special statutory rules for Sheffield marks and a Sheffield register administered by the Cutlers' Company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sheffield marks to be transferred to the Sheffield register within five years; applications, notice procedures, objections and appeals involve the Cutlers' Company and the Comptroller. Provisions for assignment, registration, refusal, appeal and punishment for counterfeiting are set out. (Refs: 114–120, 247–248, 262.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Series of Marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Series of marks may be registered; differences allowed in a series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application procedure, representations (87, 95, 237), advertisement rules (88, 240), wood-blocks, instructions and fees are specified. A series is assignable and transmissible only as a series. (Refs: 95, 237–258.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature of an Individual or Firm as Trade Mark
rubrics_metrics.description: Signature of an individual or firm may be registered as a Trade Mark provided it be the signature of the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: 90–91.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimen / Tracings / Views for Designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Specimen of Design or tracings/views may accompany application to register a Design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exact specimens or representations to be furnished before delivery of articles on sale; see rules as to drawings and instructions. (Refs: 74–75, 219–220.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Case procedure (Trade Marks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conflicting claims to a Trade Mark may be determined by a special case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may submit a special case; the Comptroller may submit or require parties to submit; the Comptroller may settle the case. Form of request and fees are prescribed. (Ref: 99, 282.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory Declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory declarations required in connection with patent applications and registering assignments of Designs or Trade Marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory Declarations Act referenced; penalty under that Act noted. Declarations appear on applications for Patents, and to register assignments (see citations: 162, 213, 243).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner to report if subsequent application is same as a prior one; prior application preferred over a subsequent one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A subsequent application for the same invention to be refused; applicants to be heard. Under the Act of 1852 the first grantee is preferred. (Refs: 10–12.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary Conviction Offences
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary convictions apply for false representations about patents, designs or trade marks and for unauthorised use of the Royal Arms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure for summary conviction in Scotland, Ireland and Isle of Man is specified; summary offences include falsely representing articles to be patented or registered, and unauthorised use of Royal Arms; penalties and references provided. (Refs: 137–139, 141, 144.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Threat of Legal Proceedings / Threatened Infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Threatened infringement of a patent may be restrained and actions for damages and injunction may follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For threat of legal proceedings reasonable and probable cause need not be shown. The Act does not apply if an action for infringement has already been commenced. (Refs: 54, 57–58.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for Specifications and other procedural times
rubrics_metrics.description: Leaving complete specification: nine months from application; accepting complete specification: twelve months from application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions apply where appeal pending. Enlargement of time for prescribed payment not to exceed three months. Sealing time for Patent: fifteen months (subject to exceptions). For Trade Marks: registering two months after advertisement but within twelve months from application (unless delay not due to applicant's default). Appeal to law officer fourteen days. (Refs: 13–14, 20–21, 25, 88–89, 182, 200.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Title in Specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Title required in a specification; the title should reflect the object of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title not to be wider than the rest of the specification and may narrow down the claim. Examiner to report on title. (Refs: 3–5.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade Mark substantive rules and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and treatment of a Trade Mark, including registration, classes, colour, goodwill attachment, assignability, exclusivity and conclusive registration after five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be registered in any colour; must be registered for a class (or part) of goods; common marks may be registered as additions; a Trade Mark is attached to goodwill and passes with goodwill; assignment and registration of assignment procedures described; registration is conclusive after five years; rectification, alteration, removal and renewal rules are set out; not entitled to registration in various circumstances (deception, scandalous, etc.). (Refs: 89–103, 110–128, 234–259.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Unregistered Trade Marks and Unregistered Assignees
rubrics_metrics.description: No proceedings can be taken to prevent or recover damages for infringement of unregistered Trade Marks, except in limited circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception for old marks where a certificate of refusal is obtained. Unregistered assignee may have rights to sue as regards a Patent and a Trade Mark in certain situations; power to assign a Trade Mark and rights of unregistered transmittee discussed. (Refs: 103–104, 123–124.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Wood-blocks and electrotypes for Trade Marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Wood-blocks or electrotypes to be furnished by applicant for a Trade Mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions as to wood-blocks and other requirements are specified. (Refs: 236, 258–259.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of prescribed Forms and Precedents
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications, notices, assignments, licences, petitions, and other processes must use prescribed forms and precedents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index lists forms and precedents for patents, designs and trade marks (applications for patent, amendment, compulsory licences, certificates, assignments, licences, mortgages, petitions for prolongation, etc.). Specific forms for many procedures are cited (e.g., forms for application to register, to rectify register, to cancel registration, to apply for compulsory licence). (See Index to Forms and Precedents, pages cited throughout: 192–206, 225–287, 306–337.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Register entries, rectification and correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Registers of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks record proprietors, licences, addresses and may be rectified or corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications exist to enter names of subsequent proprietors, to correct clerical errors, to enter new addresses, to rectify or cancel entries, and to obtain certificates or copies for use in legal proceedings. (Refs: 201–206, 227–232, 274–280.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Injunctions and interim relief
rubrics_metrics.description: Injunctions for Patents, Designs and Trade Marks may be obtained on interlocutory application and at trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orders to inspect and take samples, to continue orders, or to refuse injunctions (with account-keeping directions) are included. Forms and precedents for motions and orders are provided. (Refs: 306–319, 307–308.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificates for legal proceedings (Designs and Trade Marks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certificates of registration, refusal, or for use in legal proceedings are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms for certificate of registration of a Design, for certificate for use in legal proceedings relating to a Design, and for certificate of refusal to register an old mark are set out. (Refs: 227–229, 275, 283.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectification and saving of jurisdiction in Scotland and other jurisdictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision for rectification of registers and saving of jurisdiction of local courts (e.g., Scotland, Ireland, Isle of Man).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transmission of specifications to Scotland, rectification of registers in Scotland, definitions of 'Court' and 'Court of Appeal', proceedings for infringement and revocation in Scotland, and specific procedural variations (jury leave, assessors, 'injunction' meaning 'interdicting') are specified. (Refs: 139–141, 70.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Trusts not to be entered on Register
rubrics_metrics.description: Trusts are not to be entered on the register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an express restriction on what the public register records. (Ref: 122.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignments, licences and mortgages (form and effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignments of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks, licences to work patents, and mortgages of letters patent require prescribed forms and carry specified covenants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precedents for assignments, licences (short and longer forms), assignments of rights to foreign patents, and mortgage forms (with covenants and provisos) are included. Also agreements for sale subject to royalties and capitalistic working agreements are provided. (Refs: 320–337.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Sealing/certified copies as evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of documents sealed with the Patent Office seal and certified are receivable in evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impressions of the seal are judicially noticed; certified copies are admissible as evidence in proceedings. (Refs: 121–122, 133.)
